Low: Prune and remove lower leaves showing initial reddish-brown specks to reduce spore load.
Ensure proper weed control to reduce relative humidity around the plant base.
Monitor weather forecasts; prepare for fungicide application if prolonged wet periods are predicted.
Medium: Conduct target de-leafing of all moderately infected leaves and burn or bury the debris.
Apply protective fungicides such as Mancozeb or Chlorothalonil.
Optimize drainage channels to prevent standing water and decrease humidity in the field.
High: Perform intensive sanitation by cutting off highly infected leaves immediately.
Apply systemic fungicides (e.g., Triazoles or Strobilurins) in rotation to control active outbreaks.
Increase potassium and nitrogen fertilization to help plants produce new leaf tissue faster.
Consider replacing highly susceptible varieties with resistant hybrids in future plantings.

Low: Remove dead leaf tips showing diamond-shaped lesions.
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; use drip or under-canopy systems to keep leaves dry.
Medium: Cut away infected leaf areas showing prominent yellow halos.
Apply copper-based fungicides or Mancozeb to protect healthy foliage.
Improve plant spacing in congested blocks to allow better air circulation.
High: Remove heavily diseased leaves showing merged concentric target-like lesions.
Apply systemic fungicides in combination with a nutritional spray to boost plant defense.
Incorporate organic compost to enhance soil microbial activity and promote overall plant vigor.

Low: Continue standard agricultural practices: regular irrigation and scheduled weeding.
Conduct routine inspections every 7-10 days to spot early signs of infection.
Medium: Maintain active surveillance. A 'Medium' healthy reading might indicate a border case; verify leaf margins closely.
Ensure balanced NPK fertilization to keep the plant's immune system strong.
High: The plant is in excellent health! Maintain current cultivation and preventative hygiene measures.

Low: Quarantine the suspected plant immediately; restrict movement of people and tools near it.
Verify symptoms: check for leaf margin yellowing and petiole collapse.
Ensure all boots and tools are disinfected with a quaternary ammonium compound before leaving the zone.
Medium: Isolate the infected plant and surrounding contact plants in a 5-meter radius.
Strictly avoid moving any soil, suckers, or water from this area to other parts of the farm.
Inject the pseudostem with glyphosate to kill the plant and prevent further vascular spread.
High: Immediately eradicate the infected plant and its surrounding neighbors by burning or chemical destruction.
Fallow or quarantine the infected site; do not plant bananas in this soil for at least 5 to 10 years.
Report the outbreak to local agricultural extension offices or biosecurity departments.
For future plots, obtain certified disease-free tissue culture plantlets.

Low: Isolate the plant showing initial wilting of young internal leaves.
Bag the male inflorescence (de-budding) using a forked stick to prevent insect vector access.
Sterilize all cutting tools in 10% formaldehyde or heat before and after touching any plant.
Medium: Eradicate the infected plant immediately using systemic herbicides (e.g., Glyphosate) to dry it out in place.
Establish a buffer zone around the infected plant where no agricultural activities are performed.
Check nearby suckers for blackening or vascular discoloration.
High: Immediately destroy the infected plant, all suckers, and adjacent plants within a 6-meter radius.
Maintain a strict quarantine barrier: do not allow any animals, tools, or workers into the hot zone.
Keep the area clean-fallowed or weed-free for 12 months using herbicides to starve the soil bacteria.
Ensure strict sanitation protocols: disinfect footwear, tools, and tires at farm entry and exit points.

Low: Prune the lower leaves showing grey-centered spots.
Keep the plantation clear of weeds and decaying organic waste.
Ensure the plant has adequate fertilization to prevent stress.
Medium: Remove leaf tips and margins showing extensive lesions.
Apply protective foliar fungicides if weather is consistently wet and warm.
Control insect pests (like thrips and caterpillars) that create entry wounds on leaves.
High: Perform thorough pruning of all heavily spotted leaves and burn the waste.
Apply Mancozeb or Carbendazim foliar sprays to arrest fungal growth.
Review fertilizer scheduling: ensure adequate nitrogen and potassium to help the plant recover leaf canopy.

Low: Prune and remove lower leaves showing initial yellow streaks to prevent spore production.
Improve soil drainage in areas where water tends to collect.
Medium: Remove leaf tips showing active spots.
Apply protective foliar fungicides such as copper hydroxide or chlorothalonil.
Perform thinning to ensure proper air flow through the plant canopy.
High: Cut and destroy heavily infected leaves showing large grey centers.
Spray systemic fungicides in rotation to stop active fungal development.
Ensure balanced NPK nutrition (focusing on potassium) to support plant recovery.
